events.text: "Park deadlines must cover the acceptance runs a packet demands, not just the coding time"

**How to apply:** when writing the packet, add up what the acceptance bar makes the agent *run*, and set `--park-deadline` to comfortably exceed coding plus that. If the bar includes a command you have timed yourself, use the measured number. See [[never-amend-in-shared-futon-trees]].

**Why:** a deadline wake that fires on a job which is merely slow, not stuck, costs a round of "is it healthy?" reasoning and can trigger a needless re-dispatch. The park exists to catch silence, not to race the acceptance bar.

CLAUDE.md sets a floor of 45 min for Codex park deadlines. That floor is about the *coding*; it is not enough when the packet's own acceptance bar requires long verification runs. On 2026-09-02 claude-6 belled a packet whose acceptance demanded two ~10-minute `wm_status_report.py` runs (each launches two bounded test suites), parked at 2700s, and the deadline fired at 18:17 while the job sat in `delivering` — it had finished at 18:16:47. A third of the budget was verification, not work.

**How to apply:** before acting on an unrecognized auto-bellback, (1) check `pgrep -af 'claude -p'` for a live loop seat and read the job's prompt via `GET /api/alpha/invoke/jobs/<id>` — if the prompt is a loop row packet (e.g. "ROW TO DO THIS INVOCATION"), the LOOP owns the recovery; stand down. (2) The `?state=` filter on the jobs list endpoint is unreliable (returns terminal jobs as running) — trust only per-job GETs. (3) A park left on a cancelled job deadline-wakes later; treat that wake as a no-op check, not a re-dispatch trigger. Related: [[surfacing-reads-blocker-fields]].
"wm-build-loop work seats dispatch with --from claude-1, so their auto-bellbacks land in my session as \"your bell\" — check for a live seat before dispatching a continuation"

The wm-build-loop's headless claude work seats send agency bells attributed `--from claude-1` (the seat's own admission: unregistered callers get no bellback routing, so it borrowed my id), and their auto-bellbacks arrive in my session reading "RE: your bell" for dispatches I never made. On 2026-09-05 an F8 slice-7 bellback looked like my failed dispatch; I sent a continuation, the seat sent its own, and the seat's attempted cancel of ITS duplicate took an AGENT-LEVEL interrupt that killed MY running continuation instead — after mine had already written both Lean modules (kept by the seat, uncommitted). Work survived; one wasted round-trip plus a mis-aimed interrupt.

**Why:** the seat's identity is borrowed, a bellback carries no marker distinguishing "your dispatch" from "your seat's dispatch," and cancel interrupts at AGENT grain, not job grain — cancelling "a queued job" can kill whatever that agent is currently running.

**How to apply:** after dispatching, poll the job once (~8s) and confirm an event beyond `accepted` (`running`/`prompt`) BEFORE parking. If still `queued`, cancel (job-grain) and re-route to a seat with demonstrated throughput that day. Known-good/bad is per-day evidence, not a fixed property — codex-18 processed every job on 2026-09-06; codex-17 none. Related: [[seat-bellbacks-look-like-mine]].
"A dispatch can sit \"queued\" forever on a seat with no live worker; confirm the job reaches \"running\" (~8s) before parking on it"

On 2026-09-06 a work bell to codex-17 was accepted and then sat `queued` for an hour with a single `accepted` event — the seat is registered and roster-idle but nothing consumes its queue. The park deadline fired as a no-op wake; the same packet re-dispatched to codex-18 was `running` within seconds.

**Why:** roster `idle` status and `accepted: true` say nothing about a live worker. The CLAUDE.md corollary ("after any bell that matters, check its job state (~5s)") applies to routine work dispatches, not just unfamiliar recipients.

The library-loop lane had committed `d3c36581` in between, so the amend rewrote *their* commit (`1ac01e5e`), pulling my generator file into it. Repaired with `git reset --soft d3c36581` (the pre-amend sha from `git reflog`), then a fresh commit of my own — their commit is byte-identical again.
**Why (two incidents, same root: HEAD is not yours):**

2026-10-04, mfuton-sbcl. My new `tools/smoke.sh` ended with `git checkout -- lisp/transpiler/evidence` "to drop test churn". Run once in the shared checkout, it discarded ~22 *other agents'* uncommitted receipt edits (not in git, unrecoverable). Fixed by tar-snapshot + exact restore.

shared checkouts (futon3c, futon2, mfuton-sbcl) — `git commit -a` swept in another agent's files (2026-08-22); `--amend` rewrote another lane's commit (2026-09-05); another writer committed MY staged index (2026-09-07); a script's `git checkout -- dir` discarded ~22 uncommitted receipts (2026-10-04)

**How to apply:** `git add <paths>` then `git commit`; run `git status --short` *after* the add and expect to see your paths staged — if they are missing, someone else committed them, so find the sha with `git log -1 --stat` and report **that** sha rather than assuming your commit exists. Never `--amend` without checking `git log --oneline -1` is still your commit — prefer a follow-up commit. Never put `git checkout --`/`git restore`/`git clean` of a path into a script that may run in a shared checkout; snapshot and restore the files instead. If you do amend by mistake, `git reflog` still holds the original; `git reset --soft <original-sha>` restores it with your change left staged. Also: the Agency JVM (port 7070, Drawbridge 6768) takes `(require 'ns :reload)` via `/eval` for function bodies only — new routes must go in `futon3c.transport.http/extra-routes`, `(do …)` forms are rejected by `/eval`, and `rebuild-handler!` has no builder on the zone server. See [[park-payloads-must-not-r
In any checkout other agents are also committing to (`/home/joe/code/futon3c`, `/home/joe/code/futon2`): stage exact paths, and **re-read `git log -1` right before `--amend`**.

**Why:** brief mode means the job can complete without the server checking that tools actually ran — exactly the paraphrase-as-citation / self-report facade the lifecycle is meant to refuse. **How to apply:** `--from claude-15 --to <seat> --kind bell --mode work --park --park-deadline 2700` on every dispatch that reads code or writes files; check `GET /api/alpha/invoke/jobs/<id>` shows `mode: work` (~5 s after send). See [[formal-war-machine-locations]].
Pass --mode work on every agency_send.py dispatch that edits/commits; the server's default classifier picks "brief", which skips execution-evidence enforcement

`futon3c/scripts/agency_send.py` without `--mode work` lets the server classify the packet by regex (`http.clj` `invoke-job-mode`: only "mode: task", "task assignment", "fm-NNN", "falsify/prove/counterexample/state of play" → work); everything else runs as **brief**, which skips execution-evidence enforcement (`README-ground-control.md:40`). Discovered 2026-08-30 when D1 (P-find-over-snatch) came back `"mode":"brief"` although it writes and commits a file. The CLAUDE.md dispatch recipe does not mention the flag.
What worked: `kill -USR2 <pid>` (debug-on-event) breaks the spinning timer into *Backtrace*. `sudo ss -K` on emacs's own ports to :7070 frees the fds, but url-http sentinels then retry every request.
emacs-graph hung at 100% CPU from ~20k leaked url-http processes to :7070; SIGUSR2 unwedges; never inject Lisp via gdb

**Why:** calling `Feval` from gdb and then running `handle all nostop noprint pass` forwarded a SIGSEGV into Emacs and killed the daemon (systemd Restart=on-abnormal brought it back; the old TTY frames and REPL buffers were lost). **How to apply:** never inject Lisp through gdb into this daemon. Use gdb only for read-only `bt` and `p`. If Lisp access is needed, free fds, break with SIGUSR2, then use emacsclient. Watch `(length (process-list))` as the early warning. See [[emacs-graph-cm-abort]].

2026-09-27: the emacs-graph daemon hung after 3.8 days of uptime. It had 20,328 entries in `process-list`, mostly dead "127.0.0.1<N>" url-http connections to :7070, plus 989 idle keep-alive sockets that filled the 1024-fd limit, so emacsclient couldn't connect. make_process's unique-name loop (`name<1>`, `name<2>`, … each checked with Fget_process/assoc) is O(N²), so each `url-retrieve` from a timer took minutes.
